questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Global Institutional Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: The extent to which international organizations allow member countries to have an equal say in decision-making.

questions.a: A process involving discussion and agreement from everyone impacted by a choice, ensuring equal influence for all members.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Democratic Decision Making'.
questions.a: Consultation and consent across all spheres of life, from families to governments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Ideal Democracy Standards'.
questions.a: A goal to strive for that helps identify the weaknesses of existing systems.

questions.a: A system where all members of a small community participate directly in the decision-making process without representatives.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Political Participation Rate' refers to.
questions.a: The percentage of a specific demographic group that exercises their right to vote in an election.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Political Participation Rate'.
questions.a: Participation levels often correlate with socio-economic status.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Political Participation Rate', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: participation_rate = (voters / total_group) * 100

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Income Inequality Ratio' refers to.
questions.a: A numerical comparison showing the disparity in wealth or earnings between two different social groups.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Income Inequality Ratio'.
questions.a: Economic gaps can translate into unequal political influence.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Income Inequality Ratio', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: ratio = income_high / income_low

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Active Political Participation' refers to.
questions.a: The requirement in a democracy for citizens to engage in political activities to ensure the health of the system.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Active Political Participation'.
questions.a: The fate of a democracy depends on the actions of its citizens, not just its rulers.
